label: OmniTIK 5 PoE ac
description: MikroTik OmniTIK 5 PoE ac (RBOmniTikPG-5HacD) — 5x 1G RJ45, Wi-Fi 5 GHz. MIPSBE 1-core QCA9557.

poe.note: MikroTik prints current limits and an input-voltage range, never a watt ceiling for these four ports: PoE-out Ether2-Ether5, 1 A per port and 2 A total, at the voltage applied to the unit (11-30 V on the 100M model, 12-57 V on the ac model). Multiplying amperes by a nominal voltage would invent a figure the vendor does not publish.

notes: Inlet is `eth1` at 18 W; `eth2`-`eth5` source 802.3af/at and cannot be fed. https://mikrotik.com/product/rbomnitikpg_5hacd (read 2026-11-28): "Number of DC inputs 1 (PoE-IN)", "PoE in Passive PoE", "PoE in input Voltage 12-57 V", "Max power consumption 66 W", "Max power consumption without attachments 18 W"; "PoE-out ports Ether2-Ether5", "PoE out 802.3af/at", "Low voltage PoE-Out current limit 1 A", "High voltage PoE-Out current limit 450 mA", "Max total out (A) 2 A". https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/omnitik-series/ notes the 802.3af/at input is limited to 30 W and the unit consumes up to 15 W by itself; https://cdn.mikrotik.com/web-assets/product_files/OmniTIK_5_ac_171051.pdf prints "PoE out - Yes, Ether2 - Ether5", "1 A (if input < 30 V) / 0.5 A (if input > 30 V)", "Consumption 18 W". The budget is current x applied voltage, so it is marked unknown. Before: five silent sockets guessed at 12.95 W apiece (64.75 W) and no port declared as the PSE the datasheet says it is.
